title: EncounterLogV1
description:
The canonical on-disk artifact for one closed encounter. Written atomically
to `<logs_dir>/<started_at_unix>-<log_id>.json`.

$schema.description:
Reference to the published JSON Schema this log conforms to — the
version-keyed URL from [`schema_url`]. Lets a consumer or editor locate
and validate the document directly. Serialised first, as `$schema`.
`#[serde(default)]` keeps pre-`$schema` logs deserialisable (the current
URL is filled in on read), so this stays an additive, schema_version-1
change.

LogId.description:
Persistent unique identifier for one Encounter Log. UUIDv7 gives
time-ordered, globally-unique keys without platform dependencies.

SalvageSummary.description:
Counters that let consumers triage a log's quality at a glance without
streaming the full event list.

is_recovered.description:
True when this log was reconstructed from scratch dir at startup
(i.e. the previous session crashed or quit mid-encounter).

partial_event_count.description:
Events in `events` with `t: 1` (readable `time_ms`, some fields
missing or unreadable).

LogParticipant.description: Participant identity in the canonical log. The `t` field (0 or 1) discriminates between a fully-parsed participant and a partially-recovered one.

oneOf.description: A fully-resolved participant identity and loadout (t: 0).
A participant record where some fields could not be read (t: 1). salvaged_fields are flattened at the top level.

ParticipantHeader.description: Identity + loadout for a clean participant read.

uid.description:
Stable join key. The same `ParticipantId` the events carry as
`source_uid` / `target_uid`; an unsigned `StableUnitId` hash, NOT
the game's raw `__uid` (which the log records separately as the
top-level `hero_uid`).

talents.description:
Picked talents for hero participants: internal skill-sheet CDB row id
(e.g. `"Warrior_Hemorrhage"`) → rank (>= 1; absent key == unpicked,
matching the game's set-rank closure which removes the key at rank 0).
`BTreeMap` keeps the on-disk key order deterministic.

Best-effort: whether `HeroSpecialization.talents` is replicated for
REMOTE party-member heroes is unverified (hxbit visibility groups may
filter it), so an unreadable/empty map serialises as absent rather
than demoting the participant to Partial. `None` for NPCs.

ParticipantId.description:
Stable identity shared by a combat-log participant and every event
(`source_uid` / `target_uid`) that references it. This is the
`StableUnitId`-derived hash the bridge stamps onto each damage / heal /
shield source and target — an OPAQUE 64-bit identifier (an FNV-1a hash
over `(combat_id, spawn_tick, name)`, so the full 64-bit range is in
play and the top bit is frequently set), which is why it is carried
UNSIGNED. A participant's `uid` and an event's `source_uid` /
`target_uid` are the *same* `ParticipantId` and join by equality.

`#[serde(transparent)]` keeps the on-disk shape a bare JSON number, so
the canonical-log `schema_version` stays `1`.

## Why a named newtype

This is deliberately NOT the game's raw `__uid` (a small, sequential,
genuinely-signed `i64` that the log carries separately as `hero_uid`
and never uses as a participant/event join key). The two values live
in different namespaces.

The combat-log once serialised the participant side of the join as a
signed `i64` while the event side stayed an unsigned `u64`: for any
hash with the top bit set, the participant's `uid` came out negative
(e.g. `-6558438490268822143`) while the same entity's `source_uid`
came out positive (`11888305583440729473`) — bit-identical, but two
different JSON numbers, so consumers could never join them. Modelling
the join key as one named unsigned type makes that representation
mismatch a *compile error* rather than a silent data bug, and lets the
representation be changed in exactly one place if it ever must be.

Weapon.description:
One weapon slot in a participant's loadout.

Beyond the original `slot` + `item_id` identity pair, the live
`st.Equipment.content` walk (probe-core `hero_equipment`) fills in
per-item instance state, and the CDB catalog (when loaded) adds the
derived enrichment fields (`ilevel`, `stats`, `augment_stats`,
`upgrade_special`, `affix_factor`). Every optional field is an
`Option` with `skip_serializing_if` so pre-existing logs (and the
legacy `weaponInHand`/arsenal fallback path, which knows ids only)
keep their exact on-disk shape — schema_version stays 1.

level.description:
Per-instance item level. `None` when the instance carries the
sentinel 0, meaning "use the CDB row's level".

ilevel.description:
DERIVED: effective iLevel (def iLevel + flawless bonus + stars ×
upgrade bonus) — the input the stat generation runs at.

upgrade_level.description:
The in-game "enhancement" star count, 0..=5 (internal game field
name: `upgradeLevel`). `Some(0)` is meaningful (un-enhanced) and
is kept distinct from `None` (unreadable).

flawless.description: Bit 0 of the instance's `flags` EnumFlagsData (Flawless quality).

rarity.description:
Resolved rarity id: the per-instance override
(`st.item.Weapon.rarity`) when present, else the CDB row's rarity
(catalog-resolved). Without a loaded catalog this degrades to the
raw override only.

augments.description: Socketed augment item ids (internal game field name: `Gear.slots`).

in_hand.description:
`Some(true)` on the one equipped weapon that unambiguously matches
the hero's `weaponInHand` decode, which is tag-gated on the
`client.WeaponState` `InHand` constructor — holstered states
(`PrimaryHolster` / `SecondaryHolster`) never match. `None`
everywhere else (including when the match is ambiguous or the
venum payload is a weapon-kind row rather than the item row).

stats.description:
DERIVED: base stat lines, replayed from the game's generation
formulas. `Some([])` is meaningful — the item genuinely has no
stats; `None` means the catalog wasn't loaded at sample time.

augment_stats.description:
DERIVED: socket contributions, kept apart from `stats` so the two
sources stay distinguishable.

upgrade_special.description: DERIVED: the enhancement special, when unlocked.

affix_factor.description:
DERIVED: the slot's `affixFactor` when != 1.0 (Slot_Weapon2 =
0.4). The stat lines stay tooltip-style (unscaled).

StatLine.description:
One computed flat-attribute stat line (e.g. `Armor +286`). The values
are DERIVED: the game stores no per-item stats, it regenerates them
from `{item row, effective iLevel}`; the sampler replays that
computation via `farever-item-stats` when the CDB catalog is loaded.

UpgradeSpecial.description:
The enhancement-unlocked weapon special: granted at
`upgrade_level >= GearUpgrades.SkillUnlockLevel` (3) when the skill
`"<itemType>_Upgrade"` exists. `rank` is the 0-based resolved-rarity
index (Common 0 .. Legendary 4, no +1).

GearPiece.description:
One gear piece in a participant's loadout. Same per-instance state and
derived enrichment as [`Weapon`] minus the weapon-only `in_hand` flag
and `upgrade_special`; see the field docs there. (`rarity` here is
purely catalog-derived — gear has no instance override.)

rarity.description: DERIVED: the CDB row's rarity id (catalog-resolved).

PartialParticipantHeader.description: A participant record where some fields couldn't be read.

LogEvent.description: One chronological event in the canonical encounter log. The `t` field (0 or 1) discriminates between a fully-parsed event and a partially-recovered one.

oneOf.description: A fully-parsed combat event (t: 0). SidecarEvent fields are flattened at the top level alongside the discriminant; Option fields are omitted when None.
A partially-parsed event where time_ms was recoverable but other fields may be missing (t: 1).

SidecarEventSerde.description: Shadow of `SidecarEvent` with serde support, used for on-disk encoding.

PartialEvent.description: A timeline event with `time_ms` recoverable but some other fields missing.

BrokenEvent.description:
A record whose `time_ms` is unrecoverable; cannot be placed in the
timeline. Lives in `broken_events`, not `events`.
